key_insight: Room-temperature Ni electrodeposition joined 6061-T6 aluminum at base-metal strength through nanoscale mechanical interlocking and interfacial chemical bonding.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a low-thermal-input route for joining load-bearing aluminum components where heat-induced softening or distortion is undesirable.
method: Electrochemically texture aluminum to form a uniform nanoporous oxide layer.
Electrodeposit Ni into the nanopores and a prefabricated V-shaped groove.
Combine oxide-framework anchoring with interfacial Al–O and Ni–O bonding.
evidence_signal: Joints achieved 329 ± 6 MPa ultimate tensile strength and 100% joint efficiency, fractured in the base material, and showed no obvious base-metal grain coarsening or softened zone; XPS identified Al–O and Ni–O bonds.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish fatigue performance, corrosion durability, or scalability to larger joints.
paper_title: Electrodeposition welding for room-temperature equal-strength joining of aluminum alloys
